title: 20 · Processes, execution models, backup and archives

paras: From a program executing as a Linux process to background jobs, deadlines, threads, and durable storage operations.
Technical correction policy: detailed mechanisms, examples and verification in the corrections handbook

Source concept: “Process = running instance/object.” Technical refinement: A process is an executing program instance with a virtual address space, credentials, open file descriptors and kernel-managed resources. A thread is a schedulable execution context within a process. A process may contain several threads.

Linux connections: PID, PPID, process state, /proc , ps , top , systemctl , fork , execve , scheduling and cgroups. Compare with Chapter 19 (platform versus runtime tuning) and Chapter 16 (Linux and containers).

Your business/process note groups work into core (direct value delivery), support (HR, accounting, maintenance), and management (planning, controls, strategy). This is a business-process taxonomy , distinct from the OS-process categories above. A payroll business process can execute as a batch software process; the same word “process” operates at two levels.
Cross-link to Chapter 05 for institutions and operating models, and Chapter 06 for scheduling and operational systems. Analogy only: a department is not literally a Linux process.

Notes preserved: NAS (often SMB/NFS), SAN (often Fibre Channel/iSCSI), cloud object storage (e.g., S3 API), and archive-transfer tools such as NDMP, LTFS, rsync and SSH/SFTP. These are not interchangeable: NDMP is associated with backup data movement, LTFS with tape file organization, and rsync with file synchronization.

blocks.h2: 05 · Three independent ways to classify storage
paras: Connectivity: DAS, NAS, SAN. Data interface: file, block, object. Physical medium: HDD, SSD, magnetic tape. A NAS appliance can use HDDs or SSDs; an object-storage service can be built on many underlying media. These axes should not be merged.
